sandbox._comment: Disabled: bwrap requires unprivileged user namespaces, which our seccomp filter blocks. The container itself is the security boundary. Sub-blocks are preserved inert so this file works unchanged if ever run outside macolima.

permissions._comment: Plan interactively (prompts on, you install deps), execute autonomously (tight denies, Anthropic-only egress). acceptEdits lets Claude freely edit code but still prompts for Bash not on the allow list. The REAL boundary is the egress proxy (domain allowlist) + seccomp (no user namespaces) + non-root + cap_drop; this deny list is defense-in-depth and surface-reducing, not the boundary itself. Claude Code's Bash matcher keys off the command prefix, so denies here can be routed around by wrapper commands (env, xargs, find -exec, make targets, language interpreters running local scripts). We deny the obvious routes; the proxy catches anything that makes it through.
permissions._webfetch_note: WebFetch is intentionally NOT on the default allow list. It runs server-side at Anthropic's infrastructure and bypasses the egress-proxy entirely — every URL the agent passes to it is a potential exfil channel (the destination server logs the URL, which can carry secrets in the path/query). Add per-project WebFetch allowlists to .claude/settings.local.json scoped to specific docs domains, e.g. `WebFetch(domain:docs.numer.ai)`. WebSearch stays on because results are summaries, not arbitrary URL fetches.
permissions._read_deny_note: The Read denies below cover the Read TOOL only. They do NOT block reading the same files via Bash (`cat`, `jq`, `python /tmp/x.py`, etc.) — those are allowed below for legitimate workflow reasons. The denies still narrow the most natural read path; treat them as nudges, not gates.
permissions._acceptEdits_note: acceptEdits skips the per-edit confirmation. Combined with the /workspace bind mount this means the agent can autonomously rewrite host-visible files. Do NOT run scripts, Makefiles, or `npm`/`make` targets from /Volumes/DataDrive/repo/<profile>/ on the HOST shell — only from inside the container — or you may execute agent-authored code outside the sandbox. To require per-edit confirmation, change defaultMode to "default".
permissions._read_utilities_note: Read-only text utilities, added 2026-09-03. Measured cause: 74% of subagent Bash calls carried at least one segment head that was not on this list (echo 94, head 89, cd 78, grep 58, cut 18, tail 13 across 236 calls in one session), because the matcher evaluates EVERY segment of a compound command. Those fell through to the auto-mode classifier and were prompt-eligible; seven stalled over 20s waiting on a human, the worst for 24 minutes on `cd .. && grep -l ..`. These grant no new write reach: Bash(cat:*) already permits `cat > file`, and deny-destructive.sh blocks redirects into the sandbox's own control paths regardless of which command writes them. `sort -o` and `uniq in out` do write, and are accepted for that same reason. Shell KEYWORDS (for/while/if) can never be allow-listed by prefix and still fall through by design. `sed`/`awk` stay DENIED - they are deny-list bypasses, not pagers; use Read with offset/limit, or rg.
permissions._myclickup_note: myclickup tiers ADOPTED 2026-09-03 (work/0005 §8 item 1, owner decision), mirroring the sibling repo's claude-settings.json tier-for-tier rather than the channel's raw proposal: 21 allow / 8 ask / 2 deny against the manifest's 19 / 11 / 2. The whole difference is three writes — `comment`, `set-status`, `update` — which the channel proposes as `ask` and the sibling promoted to `allow` by owner sign-off on 2026-08-24; the owner here chose to carry that promotion (`just check-permissions` reports the three as PROMOTED, a recorded decision, not as a gap). SECURITY IMPACT: those three ClickUp writes — a comment, a status change, a task-field update — run UNPROMPTED in every profile. All three are additive or reversible against a shared workspace; none deletes an object. The remaining EIGHT writes (create/claim/tag/untag/depend/undepend/move/append-description) are absent from `allow` AND named in `ask`, and the second half is load-bearing: ABSENCE ALONE DOES NOT PRODUCE A PROMPT. Under defaultMode:auto an unlisted command is handed to a classifier whose behaviour is specified nowhere in this file and pinned by no test in this repo. The sibling verified this in a live container on 2026-08-15: a bare `myclickup create` on neither list ran unprompted (`Allowed by auto mode classifier`) and prompted once an `ask` rule existed — same command, same classifier, the rule was the only variable (see `_ask_note`). `ask` rather than `deny` for the writes because deny is absolute and would remove interactive approval, a workflow this sandbox keeps (plan interactively, execute autonomously). `Bash(myclickup:*)` would cover all 29 commands and was rejected — --dry-run is opt-in and therefore not a gate. Prefix over-matches checked against 0.7.0: `comment` over-matches `comments` (a read), `status` over-matches `statuses` (a read) but NOT `set-status`, `task` over-matches `tasks` (a read); no allowed entry is a prefix of any asked write. `delete`/`rm` are FORWARD GUARDS in `deny`: no 0.7.0 command deletes an object (`untag`/`undepend` issue HTTP DELETEs on a label and a dependency edge), and a future version that adds one arrives DENIED rather than silently permitted. Deny is the one layer verified to outrank the classifier (sibling, 2026-08-15, including the `myclickup delete --help 2>&1 | head` wrapped form — a trailing pipe does not change the prefix). The command surface is derived from the channel manifest, never transcribed by hand: the sibling carried a count that was nine commands stale by the time anyone checked. A CLI upgrade arrives by image rebuild; re-run `just check-permissions` after one and re-read this note. Accepted residual: `Bash(just:*)` and `Bash(make:*)` are allowed, so a workspace recipe wrapping a write runs unprompted.
permissions._myclickup_dryrun_note: `Bash(myclickup --dry-run:*)` is the inert form of every write, and what makes a reads-first list workable rather than merely restrictive. myclickup >= 0.2.0 accepts --dry-run BEFORE the subcommand (its ADR-0007) precisely so a prefix pattern can match it — the trailing form is indistinguishable from a live write to a prefix matcher. It prints the RESOLVED request, which matters because the permission prompt shows argv: only the dry-run reveals that --list "Team/Build/Action Items" became a list ID and a --due date became epoch-ms. It widens nothing (the reads are already allowed individually), and the sibling verified 2026-08-10 that a dry-run needs no CLICKUP_TOKEN at all — inert even before auth exists.
permissions._ask_note: `ask` forces a confirmation prompt as an explicit RULE that outranks the auto-mode classifier — verified by the sibling's differential test on 2026-08-15 (`myclickup create --help` unprompted with no ask rule, prompted with one; nothing else changed). Under defaultMode:auto a command on neither `allow` nor `deny` is decided by a classifier, not prompted by default, so every myclickup write NOT on the promoted-three list (comment/set-status/update) is named here and the design is enforced rather than assumed. These patterns match the write subcommand in FIRST position only, so they do not shadow `Bash(myclickup --dry-run:*)`: `myclickup --dry-run create …` still matches the allow entry and stays inert, while `myclickup create …` lands here. Adding a write to myclickup means adding a line here — the allow list alone does not hold the line. Every entry needs its command() twin in the agy template, where the tier is WEAKER: agy caches an approved ask as a permanent Always-Allow for the profile (see that file's _comment_ask_cache).

_hooks_comment: PreToolUse enforcement upstream of tool dispatch. The matcher-level permissions.deny list is prefix-on-tokens and cannot see destructive flags (find -delete, dd of=, etc.) or path targets (Edit to /usr/local/lib/claude-hooks/... or settings.json). The hook script handles both via regex on the full envelope. Script is baked root-owned in the image at /usr/local/lib/claude-hooks/deny-destructive.sh; agent (UID 1000) has no tool path that bypasses kernel write-protect on it. See docs/deny-destructive-hook-plan.md. NOTE: this lives at TOP level, not inside `hooks`. Claude Code validates every key inside `hooks` against its hook-event list and reports anything else as an unknown event at session start — so an annotation key belongs out here, where it is inert.
_preferences_comment: PRESERVED, NOT OWNED (ADR-0007). These three plus skipAutoPermissionPrompt, skipWorkflowUsageWarning and tui are on the convergence preserve list in scripts/profile.sh: a value already in a profile's live settings.json SURVIVES every converge, and the value here seeds a profile that does not have one yet — a fresh bootstrap, or one whose keys an earlier converge dropped. They are here for the SEEDING half only. Without a template value, `preserve` on a new profile means 'leave it unset', and the operator re-picks model and effort by hand in every profile forever. Because they are preserved rather than owned, tier-1 verify does NOT compare them (check_agent_policy_sync reads the owned list: env, hooks, permissions, sandbox), so a live value differing from these defaults is the design working, not drift. `model` is deliberately the unsuffixed id: a variant suffix pins a context window this repo has no opinion about. To force a profile back onto these defaults: scripts/profile.sh <profile> converge --defaults, which overwrites the preserved keys and captures what it replaced to claude-home/settings.discarded.json.
